record.paper_title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Best Hölder exponent for slip-boundary regularity
record.original_question: Consider weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ under the slip boundary condition u_3 = 0 and ∂u_j/∂x_3 = 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ 2. Suppose that in the region where the vorticity at both points is larger than a fixed positive constant K one has the coherence estimate sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^β, where θ(x,y,t) is the angle between the vorticities at x and y and β lies in [0, 1/2]. What is the smallest exponent β for which this geometric assumption alone, without additional hypotheses such as ω ∈ L^2(0,T;L^r), is sufficient to guarantee regularity? In particular, can the threshold be improved below β = 1/2?

evidence.quote: The central and more challenging open problem is the improvement of the best exponent β for which the assumption (2.9) guarantees the regularity of the solutions without any other additional hypotheses.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u − Δu + ∇p = 0,   ∇·u = 0,
in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ = { x = (x_1,x_2,x_3) : x_3 > 0 }, on a time interval (0,T), under the slip (Navier-type) boundary conditions
  u_3(x_1,x_2,0,t) = 0,    ∂u_j/∂x_3 (x_1,x_2,0,t) = 0   for j = 1,2,
together with a smooth, divergence-free, compatible initial datum u(·,0) = u_0. Let ω = curl u denote the vorticity, and for points x,y ∈ Ω with ω(x,t) ≠ 0 and ω(y,t) ≠ 0 let θ(x,y,t) ∈ [0,π] be the angle between ω(x,t) and ω(y,t).

Fix a constant K > 0 and a constant β ∈ [0, 1/2]. Suppose u is a Leray–Hopf weak solution satisfying the geometric coherence condition: there exists c > 0 such that for almost every t ∈ (0,T) and for all x, y ∈ Ω with |ω(x,t)| > K and |ω(y,t)| > K one has
  sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c |x − y|^β.        (∗)

It is known that under the additional integrability hypothesis ω ∈ L^2(0,T; L^r(Ω)) (for an appropriate r depending on β), condition (∗) implies that u is strong, hence regular, on [0,T]; and that for β = 1/2 the additional hypothesis is superfluous, i.e. (∗) alone yields regularity.

Determine the infimum of values β ∈ [0, 1/2] for which condition (∗) by itself, with no further integrability assumption on ω, suffices to guarantee that u is regular on [0,T]. In particular, decide whether the threshold β = 1/2 can be lowered: does there exist β < 1/2 such that (∗) alone implies regularity?
artifact.category_tag: Navier–Stokes regularity criteria via vorticity direction
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent surveys and research on vorticity-direction regularity criteria (e.g., Beirão da Veiga–Berselli works, Grujić et al. localizations) continue to treat β = 1/2 as the best known unconditional Hölder exponent for the slip boundary case; later papers explicitly list improving this exponent below 1/2 as an open problem. No source verifies that the threshold has been lowered, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Regularity under slip/Navier boundary conditions assuming 1/2-Hölder coherence of the vorticity direction.
